puzzles.title: Part A
puzzles.narrative_intro: Cho: "The maintenance guy says he was fixing a heater in the workshop. He even photographed it for his report. Problem is, nobody's clock in this lodge tells the right time."

body.text: Evidence: The maintenance workshop is behind the staff block, a 7-minute walk from the spa.

lines: Owen's photo of the heater has a timestamp from his phone: 9:39.
His phone is 4 minutes slow. He never fixed it.
The workshop wall clock is visible in the photo, showing 9:49.
That wall clock is 6 minutes fast.

prompt.question: What was the real time when the photo was taken?

puzzles.title: Part B
puzzles.narrative_intro: Cho: "The spa wing's outer door was locked at 9:30, and only the spa key opens it. The key cabinet has three envelopes, and somebody's idea of a joke was to swap the labels. Every label is wrong."

body.text: The three envelopes are labelled SPA, WORKSHOP and SPA + WORKSHOP.
Each one holds exactly what one of the labels says: the spa key, the workshop key, or both keys.

lines: The envelope labelled SPA + WORKSHOP turned out to hold only the spa key.
Owen signed out the envelope labelled SPA.

prompt.question: Which key was inside the envelope Owen signed out?

puzzles.handoff: "Cho closes the file. Rigsby's found an old phone note from the sister."

puzzles.title: Part A
puzzles.narrative_intro: Rigsby: "The sister texted her manager at 9:30, using the old phone-keypad style: tap a key once for its first letter, twice for its second, and so on."

body.text: Evidence: The radio room is at the top of the main building, an 8-minute walk from the spa. During the storm it's used to talk to the mountain rescue team.

puzzles.title: Part B
puzzles.narrative_intro: Rigsby: "The mountain rescue coordinator sent us a coded message about her. Rescue teams use a grid code. Their square starts with the word RESCUE, then the rest of the alphabet."

body.text: The first digit is the row, the second is the column. I and J share a cell.

prompt.question: What does the coordinator's message say?

puzzles.handoff: "Rigsby bags the note. Van Pelt's got the rink coach's notebook. The instructor's next."

puzzles.title: Part A
puzzles.narrative_intro: Van Pelt: "The ski instructor says he was training on the outdoor ice rink, a 9-minute walk from the spa. His coach was there, and she writes her notes in a code based on the rink's rules sign."

body.label: Evidence: The coach's note about tonight's session reads:

body.text: The rules sign at the rink gate:

items: Skates must be laced tight before stepping onto the ice.
No food or drinks past the red rope.
Lessons run every evening from seven until ten.
Please stop at the gate and show your card.
Report any cracks to the rink office at once.

prompt.question: What does the coach's note say about how Mateo skated?

puzzles.title: Part B
puzzles.narrative_intro: Van Pelt: "A coach's word is good. A sensor's is better. The lodge's motion panel stores which zones had movement as a single number, and each zone is one bit."

prompt.question: Which zone had movement in all three readings?

puzzles.handoff: "Van Pelt closes the logs. Lisbon's got the library PC."

puzzles.title: Part A
puzzles.narrative_intro: Lisbon: "The negotiator says she was working on the library PC. The spa is a 5-minute walk from the library each way, so she'd need at least 10 minutes away to do it."

body.text: Evidence: The library PC records who is logged in every 3 minutes from 9:35 to 9:50.

prompt.question: The program only prints "Login audit done." What is the value of mine when it finishes?

puzzles.title: Part B
puzzles.narrative_intro: Lisbon: "So someone else was on her PC at 9:44. Her phone's step counter shows she was walking between two times. How long was she gone?"

prompt.question: The program only prints "Steps checked." What is the value of gone when it finishes?
